title: Lens Flare with Light Source Tracking & Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a lens flare post-processing effect with a movable light source and a physics debug overlay. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Create a scene with a dark blue/black background (color #0a0a1a)
- Add a ground plane (50x50 units) with a grid material at y=0
- Place 5 metallic spheres (radius 1) at positions: (-6,1,0), (-3,1,0), (0,1,0), (3,1,0), (6,1,0)
- Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 20) looking at origin
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation

## Light Source & Lens Flare
- Create a PointLight (color #ffffcc, intensity 2.0) starting at position (10, 15, 5)
- Attach a visible sphere mesh (radius 0.5, emissive material matching light color) to represent the light
- Implement a custom lens flare effect using screen-space calculations:
  - Project the light position to screen coordinates each frame
  - Render 4 flare elements (hexagonal sprites) along the line from light screen-pos through screen center
  - Flare elements should have decreasing opacity (0.8, 0.5, 0.3, 0.15) and increasing size
  - Flare visibility should be 0 when light is behind camera or occluded
- The light orbits automatically: x = 10*cos(time*0.5), z = 10*sin(time*0.5), y stays at 15

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Implement a toggleable debug overlay (DOM-based, id='debug-overlay') showing:
  - Light world position (x, y, z) with 2 decimal places
  - Light screen position (NDC x, y) with 3 decimal places
  - Flare visibility (0.0 to 1.0)
  - Current flare element count visible
  - FPS counter
- The overlay should be a semi-transparent dark panel in the top-right corner
- Toggle with 'D' key

## User Interactions
- Press 'P' to pause/resume the light orbit animation
- Press 'I' to increase light intensity by 0.5 (max 5.0)
- Press 'O' to decrease light intensity by 0.5 (min 0.5)
- Press 'F' to toggle flare effect on/off
- Press 'D' to toggle debug overlay visibility
- Press 'R' to reset light to initial position and intensity
- Click on any sphere to highlight it (emissive glow) and make the light point toward it

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- lightPosition: {x, y, z} - current world position of light
- lightScreenPos: {x, y} - NDC coordinates of light on screen (-1 to 1 range)
- lightIntensity: number - current intensity value
- flareVisible: boolean - whether flare elements are currently rendered
- flareEnabled: boolean - whether flare effect is toggled on
- flareElementCount: number - number of visible flare elements (0-4)
- animationPaused: boolean - whether orbit is paused
- debugOverlayVisible: boolean - whether debug panel is shown
- selectedSphere: number|null - index (0-4) of clicked sphere or null
- fps: number - current frames per second
- frameCount: number - total frames rendered
- lightBehindCamera: boolean - true if light is behind camera frustum
- flareOpacities: number[] - array of 4 current flare element opacities

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Light orbit must follow circular path x=10*cos(t*0.5), z=10*sin(t*0.5), y=15. Flare screen positions must be computed via proper MVP projection. Flare visibility must be 0 when dot(cameraForward, lightDirection) < 0. Intensity must be clamped [0.5, 5.0]. Flare opacities scale linearly with base visibility.
